title: Born with zero artistic skills, help this poor dev
author: Perseus38
selftext:
Hi



I'm a game developer and I'm creating a 2D action RPG with a top-down view using pixel art. Everything was working well until now, when I needed some assets for my game.



I know there are amazing assets free and paid on some websites, but I need something more customized so I started creating some assets using Aseprite, starting with my main character. But then I understood why creating a simple pixel art game takes so much time: it's very frustrating having to recreate a single animation for each of the 8 directions (I know that 3 can simply be mirrored and that's it, but 5 variations for each animation still too much for me). And here I am, asking for help to find a more efficient way to create pixel art.



Things I've already tried/used, but didn't work very well:



. Smack Studio

. 3D modeling using Blender to texture the pixel art



I know I'm being a bit too "lazy" in wanting simple things, but art is really my weak point and it's what's preventing me from improving in that area. I've tried countless times to overcome this obstacle in the past, but it doesn't work; the most I can manage is creating a good sprite after weeks of work (a single one, not an animation, and certainly not a complete spritesheet).

comments.author: Cristazio
comments.body: I heard RetroDiffusion and PixelLab are quite good. I'm not 100% sure but I think there are some non-AI tools that can help in turning 3D models into pixel art

comments.author: Catalysst
comments.body:
Yep art is definitely a struggle, I've tried a bunch of AI pixel art generators but they are pretty meh so far

My plan is move on with crappy placeholder art and when the project really comes together will connect with actual pixel artists for nicer stuff if I actually want to finish it off

It's good to do a dive into it yourself though so you can get a rough idea of exactly how many sprites and exactly what animations they need, what you want your game resolution to be etc. just so you don't code yourself into a corner

"If I was going to draw everything, what is the bare minimum"
If you want to do it through AI, you need to answer those questions for yourself anyway.

Your other option is to build the game around it, find a way to minimize your need for animations or a way that makes it easier for you to create the assets that still works within the game lore/idea.

It might mean a decent re-think but at least you're planning ahead
